verdicts.title: Recent advances on the log-rank conjecture in communication complexity
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: The log-rank conjecture is one of the fundamental open problems in communication complexity. It speculates that the deterministic communication complexity of any two-party function is equal to the log of the rank of its associated matrix, up to polynomial factors. Despite much research, we still know very little about this conjecture. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract describes a survey on the log-rank conjecture relating deterministic communication complexity to log of matrix rank, but says nothing about a 'geometric measure' defined via Fourier coefficient volumes or any linear Θ(Rank) correlation with such a measure.

verdicts.title: Structure of sparse Boolean functions over Abelian groups, and its application to testing

It shares the Fourier-analytic vocabulary but does not address the specific GeoMeasure(f) = Θ(Rank(M_f)) claim.

verdicts.title: Applications of Monotone Rank to Complexity Theory
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Raz's recent result \cite{Raz2010} has rekindled people's interest in the study of \emph{tensor rank}, the generalization of matrix rank to high dimensions, by showing its connections to arithmetic formulas.
